problem_text:
A logistics coordinator is assembling a fleet of autonomous delivery drones for a three-phase urban resupply mission. They must select a combination of payload modules to maximize total utility points while adhering to the aggregate lift capacity constraint.

The available modules are:
* Module A: mass 2kg, utility 256 points
* Module B: mass 10kg, utility 115 points
* Module C: mass 22kg, utility 36 points
* Module D: mass 6kg, utility 268 points
* Module E: mass 34kg, utility 140 points
* Module F: mass 9kg, utility 143 points
* Module G: mass 22kg, utility 227 points
* Module H: mass 8kg, utility 210 points
* Module I: mass 45kg, utility 12 points
* Module J: mass 47kg, utility 155 points
* Module K: mass 36kg, utility 163 points
* Module L: mass 27kg, utility 172 points
* Module M: mass 32kg, utility 167 points
* Module N: mass 4kg, utility 18 points
* Module O: mass 32kg, utility 75 points
* Module P: mass 8kg, utility 26 points
* Module Q: mass 14kg, utility 138 points
* Module R: mass 15kg, utility 71 points
* Module S: mass 41kg, utility 275 points
* Module T: mass 15kg, utility 107 points
* Module U: mass 33kg, utility 161 points
* Module V: mass 28kg, utility 160 points
* Module W: mass 30kg, utility 254 points
* Module X: mass 40kg, utility 224 points
* Module Y: mass 14kg, utility 114 points
* Module Z: mass 44kg, utility 12 points
* Module AA: mass 46kg, utility 120 points
* Module BB: mass 24kg, utility 95 points

Furthermore, due to compatibility protocols, precisely one of Module A or Module B must be included in the configuration.

If Module C is selected, it necessitates a dedicated support system that reduces the effective total lift capacity by 10 kg.
The maximum allowable aggregate mass for the mission is 481 kg. The coordinator must determine the optimal selection of modules.
